issues.description: Array helper method name is inconsistent across provided artifacts: the template defines ArrayHelpers.appendElement(T[], T) but Stock.addToStockIngredients(...) in the template calls ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray(...), which does not exist in the template (it exists only in the solution). This causes a compilation error in the starter code and also confuses students about which helper API they are supposed to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template compile and unify the API name: either rename template ArrayHelpers.appendElement(...) to addElementToArray(...), or add a new addElementToArray(...) method in the template that delegates to appendElement(...), and update template call sites consistently.

issues.description: Problem statement contradicts itself about SealSaloon.stock: it first says SealSaloon has a final Stock stock initialized in the SealSaloon constructor, but later explicitly requires stock to be static (shared across all instances). These requirements cannot both be satisfied as written (constructor-initialized instance field vs. shared static field).
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended design in the problem statement. If inventory is shared, specify 'private static final Stock stock = new Stock();' and remove the instruction to initialize stock in the constructor as an instance field.

issues.description: Problem statement UML vs. text disagree on whether SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...) is static: the UML shows it as an instance method, while the text explicitly requires it to be static (shared-stock management). Students may implement the wrong modifier and fail tests expecting the static signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the UML to mark acceptSupplyDelivery as static (e.g., add {static} or UML static notation) so it matches the written requirement and the expected implementation.
